claims.text: Resistance of HEAs to combined wear and corrosion is governed by dynamic formation and rapid self-healing of a multicomponent passive oxide/hydroxide film.
Mechanical stress causes local elemental segregation that enriches passivation-promoting elements such as Cr and Al at exposed surfaces.
Surface enrichment in passivation-promoting elements enables repeated removal and regeneration of the passive film.
Repeated passive-film regeneration can make combined degradation lower than the sum of independent wear and corrosion losses.
The proposed initial material is a homogeneous, disordered HEA solid solution containing a significant fraction of passivation-promoting elements.
The controlled comparison applies simultaneous sliding and corrosion, wear-only exposure, and corrosion-only exposure to matched samples.
Cyclic rest intervals permit partial reformation of the passive film.
Wear must be moderate enough to permit repassivation during the proposed test.
The structural mediator is an adaptive mixed oxide/hydroxide surface film enriched in passivating elements at wear-exposed regions.
Mechanical wear locally removes the native oxide film.
The HEA's multicomponent chemistry drives rapid film reformation through elemental segregation and oxidation.
Repassivation counteracts material loss that would otherwise arise from independent wear and corrosion.
Under simultaneous wear-corrosion, net material loss will be significantly lower than the sum of wear-only and corrosion-only losses.
The baseline is the sum of independently measured wear-only and corrosion-only losses from a similar HEA with a less optimized passivating composition.
The predicted benefit holds only when passive-film regrowth can keep pace with mechanical removal.
Sufficient oxygen or another oxidizing agent is required for the proposed film-formation mechanism.
The prediction may fail at extreme mechanical loads because film removal can outpace film regrowth.
The prediction may fail in inert environments because oxidation is suppressed.
The effectiveness of repassivation may vary with sliding speed, load, and environmental composition.
A simultaneous loss equal to or greater than the sum of independent wear-only and corrosion-only losses would falsify the proposed adaptive-repassivation explanation.

contradictions.description: The intervention calls for matched samples, but the stated baseline sums independent losses from a different, less-optimized HEA. The falsification design includes both optimized and control alloys without specifying which alloy supplies the independent-loss sum. Consequently, the comparison underlying the prediction and falsification rule is internally inconsistent and could confound composition with test mode.
